subject: Capstone compute for small college — request for pilot credits and short extension
messages:
From: Elias Novak <elias@norbridge.edu>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Small-college capstone compute — quick ask

Hi Lauren,

I'm Elias Novak, faculty lead for the CS capstone at Norbridge College (small liberal arts, ~1,800 undergrads). We're running a student project this winter where each team (around 10 teams, ~20 students total) will fine-tune and evaluate a compact LLM assistant on campus-collected transcripts. Budget is very tight — department can cover incidental costs but not cloud compute.

Would Redwood consider a short pilot credit allocation or a trial extension so students can finish model runs and evaluations? We're aiming for a 10-week window (early Jan to mid-Mar), and expect occasional bursts (a few concurrent runs during demo week). Data is non-sensitive and consented to for research.

Attached is a short project outline to help evaluate scope. Ideally we'd like anything between $1,000–$2,500 in credits or a 3-month trial extension — whatever is feasible on your side. Happy to jump on a 20–30 min call to discuss constraints.

Thanks for considering this — it would make a big difference for undergrads who otherwise can't access GPU credits.

Best,
Elias Novak
Associate Professor, Computer Science
Norbridge College
[attachment: capstone_outline.pdf (pdf, 92KB)]
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Elias Novak <elias@norbridge.edu>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 12:05:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Small-college capstone compute — quick ask

Hi Elias — thanks for the note and the outline, appreciated.

Quick clarifying Qs so I can route this internally:
- Do the student runs require GPU instances with sequence lengths > 2k, or are most experiments short-context (<=1k)?
- Will the models be public open checkpoint variants (e.g., Llama/OPT family) or custom weights?
- Do you need an uninterrupted 3-month window, or would you accept two separate credit allocations across Jan and Mar?

If you could fill out this short intake (one page) it helps speed approvals: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSfCapstoneIntake

I'll loop in our education programs and AR/account rep once I have that. We often can offer pilot credit bundles plus a short trial extension for academic classes.

— Lauren Bishop
Senior Solutions Manager, Education Programs
Redwood Inference
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: Elias Novak <elias@norbridge.edu>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:20:00 -05:00
Subject: Fwd: Small-college capstone compute — request from Norbridge (summary + ask)

Marissa / Ben — forwarding Elias's request from Norbridge College (attached outline). TL;DR: small undergrad program, ~20 students, 10 teams, non-sensitive transcripts, need credits or trial extension spanning Jan–Mar for fine-tuning and evaluation. Budget constrained.

My read: Candidate for an education pilot allocation. Recommended offer: 3-month trial extension + $1,500 in pilot credits (to be used on hosted API or Dedicated trial), plus a 30-min onboarding session. If procurement requires a PO, we can provide a quote and a DocuSign acceptance.

Notes:
- If sequence lengths are mostly <=1k this $1.5k should be sufficient for prototyping and grading runs; if they need long contexts we should bump estimate.
- Let's put standard EDU usage terms (non-commercial research only).

Requested next steps: Ben, can you prepare a brief quote + DocuSign envelope? Marissa, any precedent for similar-sized classes and what we typically allot?

Thanks — looping Elias on the internal thread for transparency.

Attachment: capstone_outline.pdf
From: Elias Novak <elias@norbridge.edu>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 14:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Small-college capstone compute — request from Norbridge (summary + ask)

Hi Lauren / Marissa / Ben —

Thanks for the quick response and for considering this. Sequence lengths will be mixed but mostly short (<1k); a couple of evaluation runs may use longer contexts but they are occasional. We completed the intake form (just submitted).

A 3-month extension + $1,500 sounds excellent and workable for our grading timeline. Procurement at Norbridge will want a short quote and a DocuSign to sign authority — I can route that once you send it.

I've attached a signed departmental approval PDF (low-level approval) to speed procurement. Please let me know any next steps and I can provide PO info quickly.

Best,
Elias
